title: Cell culture and neuronal differentiation
description: Neural stem cells Cor3-1 were cultured in complete media with supplements and growth factors. For neuronal differentiation, cells were transferred to priming and differentiation media with specific supplements and growth factors over several days.
goal: to culture neural stem cells and induce neuronal differentiation

title: Huwe1 knock-out via adenovirus transduction
description: Neural stem cells with floxed Huwe1 were transduced with adenovirus expressing CRE recombinase at MOI 100 to induce knock-out. Control cells were transduced with empty adenovirus at the same MOI.
goal: to knock out Huwe1 gene in neural stem cells

title: P19 cell culture and differentiation
description: P19 cells were maintained in MEM-α with supplements and differentiated by transferring to Neurobasal medium with supplements. Differentiation medium was changed every 24 hours as needed.
goal: to culture and differentiate P19 cells

title: P19 cell transfection with Lipofectamine 2000
description: P19 cells at 80% confluence were transfected with plasmid DNA using Lipofectamine 2000 at a 1:2 DNA to Lipofectamine ratio in proliferation medium following manufacturer instructions.
goal: to transfect P19 cells with plasmid DNA

title: Quantitative Real-Time PCR
description: Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed to cDNA. qRT-PCR was performed using SYBR Green master mix with EiF1α as housekeeping gene. Thermal cycling conditions were specified.
goal: to quantify gene expression levels

title: Western blotting from total and fractionated lysates
description: Proteins were extracted from cells, quantified, separated by SDS-PAGE, transferred to membranes, blocked, and probed with primary and secondary antibodies. Detection was performed using ECL reagents.
goal: to detect specific proteins by western blot
key_materials: primary antibodies (Ascl1, Histone H3, α-Tubulin, LaminB, Huwe1)
secondary antibodies (goat anti-mouse HRP, rabbit IgG HRP)

title: Cellular fractionation of Cor3-1 and P19 cells
description: Cells were washed, pelleted, and sequentially lysed with buffers E1, E2, and E3 to separate cytoplasm, nucleus, and chromatin fractions. Chromatin fraction was sonicated or digested for downstream analysis.
goal: to separate cellular components into cytoplasm, nucleus, and chromatin fractions
key_materials: E1 buffer (Hepes-KOH, NaCl, EDTA, glycerol, NP-40, Triton X-100, DTT)

title: Agarose-TUBEs pull down of ubiquitylated proteins
description: Ubiquitylated proteins were pulled down from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions using Agarose-TUBEs. Bound proteins were eluted and analyzed by SDS-PAGE alongside unbound and input fractions.
goal: to isolate ubiquitylated proteins from cell fractions

title: Obtain ethics approval for human specimen use
description: The use of human specimens was approved by the Ethics Reviewing Board of the University Hospital of Liege, Belgium in 2020 (ref. 2020/119).
goal: to obtain ethical approval for use of human specimens

title: Collect and select human postmortem biopsies
description: Lung postmortem biopsy specimens from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients were collected and matched by age and sex. Additional biopsies from liver, heart, kidney, and pancreas were obtained from COVID-19 patients. All tissues were selected by two pathologists after H&E staining.
goal: to collect and select human tissue samples for analysis
key_materials: Biobank of the Liege University Hospital

title: Retrospective analysis of hematology and biochemistry
description: Hematology and blood biochemistry data of COVID-19 patients were retrospectively analyzed using the last available blood sample taken within 24 hours before death. Biomarkers were analyzed by the central laboratory of the Liege University Hospital.
goal: to analyze hematology and biochemistry of COVID-19 patients

title: Prepare FFPE tissue sections for histology and immunofluorescence
description: Samples were formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded (FFPE). Serial 4 µm tissue sections were cut for histological and immunofluorescence examination.
goal: to prepare tissue sections for histological and immunofluorescence analysis

title: Digitize H&E-stained whole tissue slides
description: H&E-stained whole slides were digitized using a Pannoramic 250 Flash III Scanner to obtain high-resolution images for further analysis.
goal: to digitize histological slides for image analysis

title: Histopathological scoring of lung lesions
description: High-resolution images focused on immunofluorescence-detected NET areas were assessed by two pathologists using a scoring system for lesions typical of SARS-CoV-2 diffuse alveolar damage in various lung compartments.
goal: to score lung tissue lesions associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection

title: Prepare lung tissue sections for immunofluorescence
description: Lung tissues were formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) and cut into 4-µm-thick sections. Sections were deparaffinized, rehydrated, boiled in sodium carbonate buffer for antigen retrieval, and permeabilized in PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100.
goal: to prepare lung tissue sections suitable for immunofluorescence staining

title: Block and stain lung sections with primary antibodies
description: Tissue sections were incubated with blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature, then stained with rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 and goat anti-human MPO antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
goal: to label NET markers citrullinated histone H3 and MPO in lung sections
key_materials: PBS with 2% BSA and 2% donkey serum
rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 antibody (Abcam, Ab5103)
goat anti-human MPO antibody (R&D Systems, AF3667)

title: Grow tomato plants under controlled conditions
description: Four-week-old tomato plants were germinated in vermiculite under specific light, temperature, and humidity conditions. Seedlings were irrigated with Hoagland solution or modified nutrient solutions lacking nitrogen and supplemented with different nitrogen sources. pH was adjusted to 6.0.
goal: to grow tomato plants under defined nutrient and environmental conditions

title: Apply PA biosynthesis inhibitors and Put treatments
description: Inhibitor solution containing DFMA and DFMO was applied to pots one week before Pst inoculation. Put treatment involved foliar spraying of 0.5 mM Put or mock solution 48 hours before infection.
goal: to inhibit PA biosynthesis or apply Putrescine prior to pathogen inoculation

title: Culture and inoculate Pseudomonas syringae
description: Pst and COR- strain were grown in KB medium with antibiotics. Bacterial suspensions were prepared and used to dip inoculate tomato leaves. Disease rate was scored at 72 hours post-inoculation.
goal: to infect tomato plants with Pseudomonas syringae for disease assays

title: Culture and prepare Botrytis cinerea spores
description: B. cinerea was cultured on PDA at 24 °C. Spores were collected from 10-15 day old cultures, filtered, quantified, and adjusted to 1×10^6 spores/ml.
goal: to prepare Botrytis cinerea spores for bioassays

title: Measure biomass, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic rate
description: Dried plant tissues were weighed for biomass. Chlorophyll content was measured using a SPAD meter. Net photosynthetic rate was measured on mature leaves using an infrared gas analyser under controlled light and airflow.
goal: to assess plant biomass, chlorophyll levels, and photosynthetic performance

title: Determine H2O2 accumulation and perform microscopy
description: Leaves were stained with DAB to visualize H2O2 accumulation and destained. DAB staining intensity was quantified from micrographs. H2O2 was also quantified using the xylenol orange method from leaf disc extracts.
goal: to detect and quantify hydrogen peroxide accumulation in leaves

title: Analyze gene expression by qRT-PCR
description: RNA was extracted from leaf tissue, treated with DNase, and reverse transcribed to cDNA. qRT-PCR was performed using specific primers and SYBR Green detection. EF1α was used as housekeeping control.
goal: to quantify gene expression changes in tomato leaves

title: Analyze stomatal aperture by microscopy
description: Leaves were inoculated with Pst, and epidermal impressions were made using dental resin and nail polish. Stomatal apertures were imaged by light microscopy and measured using image analysis software.
goal: to measure stomatal aperture changes after pathogen inoculation

title: Replace fliG gene with pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele
description: The fliG gene on the Salmonella chromosome was replaced by a pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele using the λ Red homologous recombination system as described previously.
goal: to replace the fliG gene with a fluorescently tagged allele

title: Prepare bacterial growth media
description: L broth was prepared as described before. T broth contained 10 g of Bacto tryptone and 5 g of NaCl per liter. Ampicillin and arabinose were added to the medium at final concentrations of 100 µg/ml and 0.02% (wt/vol), respectively.

title: Perform DNA manipulations and sequencing
description: DNA manipulations were carried out as described before. DNA sequencing reactions were performed using BigDye v3.1 according to the manufacturer's instructions and analyzed by a 3130 Genetic Analyzer.

title: Conduct flagellar protein export assay
description: Salmonella cells were grown in LB to OD600 ~1.0, washed with motility buffer, and incubated at 30°C for 1 hour. Cells and supernatants were separated by centrifugation. Proteins from supernatants were precipitated with trichloroacetic acid, resuspended in loading buffer, heated, and analyzed by SDS-PAGE followed by immunoblotting with anti-FlgD and anti-FliC antibodies.
goal: to assess flagellar protein export

title: Purify pHluorin(M153R) and pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His proteins
description: pHluorin(M153R) was purified from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007. pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His was purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013.

title: Fluorescence microscopy of Salmonella cells
description: Salmonella cells expressing various pHluorin fusion proteins were observed using a custom-built fluorescence microscope system with specific excitation filters and a high-speed wavelength switcher. Fluorescent images were captured by an EMCCD camera controlled by MetaMorph 3.6 software.

title: Determination of cytoplasmic pH using pH imaging
description: Bulk and local cytoplasmic pH of Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin variants were determined from the fluorescence intensity ratio at 410-nm and 470-nm excitation wavelengths. Images were captured with 1 s exposure and analyzed after background subtraction and smoothing using image processing software. pH values were calculated using standard curves from purified proteins.
goal: to determine cytoplasmic pH of Salmonella cells

title: Determination of local pH around export apparatus
description: Fluorescence images with 5 s exposure were used to measure the fluorescence intensity of single pHluorin(M153R)-FliG spots after background subtraction. Local pH was calculated from the 410/470 fluorescence ratio using calibration curves from purified protein and in vivo calibration with a Salmonella mutant strain treated with gramicidin and potassium benzoate at various external pH values.
goal: to determine local pH around the export apparatus

title: Culture primary human astrocytes
description: Primary human astrocytes were expanded in Human Astrocyte Media supplemented with FBS, penicillin streptomycin, and Astrocyte Growth Supplement. Prior to experiments, astrocytes were cultured in a 50:50 mix of F10:MEMα media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin streptomycin.

title: Reduce IGF1R levels in astrocytes
description: Astrocytes were treated with 11 μg/ml MAB391 for 24 hours to reduce IGF1R levels. After treatment, cells were washed with PBS and cultured for a further 72 hours in fresh media. An IgG isotype control was included.
goal: to reduce IGF1R levels in astrocytes

title: Culture and differentiate LUHMES cells
description: LUHMES cells were grown in proliferation medium containing DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX, N2 supplement, and FGF. At 50-60% confluence, cells were differentiated by replacing media with differentiation media containing tetracycline. After two days, cells were trypsinized and replated for an additional three days to become fully differentiated.

title: Generate GFP LUHMES cells
description: Non-differentiated LUHMES cells were transduced with LV-GFP for 24 hours. Media were then replaced with fresh proliferation media and cells were cultured for 72 hours before experiments.

title: Culture fibroblasts as control cells
description: Fibroblasts were cultured in Minimum essential medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% MEM vitamins, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 60 μg/ml uridine. They were used as controls to ensure neurite outgrowth effects were specific to astrocytes.

title: Set up astrocyte-LUHMES co-cultures
description: Astrocytes were seeded onto fibronectin-coated plates and LUHMES were differentiated separately. After two days, LUHMES were replated onto astrocytes and co-cultured for 24 hours in differentiation media. Co-cultures with fibroblasts were set up similarly with higher fibroblast seeding density.

title: Co-culture with MAB391-treated astrocytes
description: Astrocytes were seeded and treated with MAB391 or MAB002 for 24 hours. GFP LUHMES were then replated onto treated astrocytes, and antibodies were removed. Co-cultures were maintained for 72 hours before treatment with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.

title: Prepare astrocyte lysates
description: After treatments, cells were washed with ice-cold PBS and lysed in extra strong lysis buffer containing detergents and inhibitors. Lysates were incubated on ice, sonicated, centrifuged, and protein concentration was determined using a BCA assay.

title: In vitro expansion of CD8+CD28− T cells
description: CD8+CD28− T cells were generated by stimulating enriched A-CD8+ T cells with B-APCs in the presence of IL-2, IL-7, and IL-15 for 9 days in 24-well plates.
goal: to generate in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells

title: Co-culture suppression assay of CD4+ T cell proliferation
description: CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells were co-cultured with B-APCs or I-APCs in the presence or absence of in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells for 7 and 11 days to assess suppression of CD4+ T cell proliferation by CFSE dilution assay.
goal: to assess the suppressive capacity of in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells on CD4+ T cell proliferation

title: In vivo suppression assay in NOG mice
description: A mixture of human cells including APCs and CD8+CD28− T cells was injected intraperitoneally into NOG mice. After 11 days, spleens were analyzed by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry to evaluate suppression of human CD4+ T cell proliferation.
goal: to investigate the stability of allogeneic suppressive capacity of CD8+CD28− T cells in vivo

title: Proliferation assay of CD8+ T cell subsets with cytokines
description: The proliferative capacity of CD8+CD28+ and CD8+CD28− T cells was measured by CFSE dilution after stimulation with APCs in the presence of common gamma chain cytokines for 9 days.
goal: to examine proliferation differences of CD8+ T cell subsets in response to cytokines
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Induction of CD8+CD28− T cells from CD8+CD28+ T cells
description: Purified CD8+CD28+ T cells were cultured with common gamma chain cytokines to observe the generation of CD8+CD28− T cells over time.
goal: to determine if common gamma chain cytokines promote transformation of CD8+CD28+ to CD8+CD28− T cells
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Annexin V staining for cell survival analysis
description: Cell death rates of CD8+CD28+ and CD8+CD28− T cells were evaluated by Annexin V staining after 9 days incubation with or without common gamma chain cytokines.
goal: to evaluate the effect of cytokines on survival of CD8+ T cell subsets
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Phenotypic analysis of cytokine receptor expression
description: Expression levels of cytokine receptors CD215, CD122, CD25, and CD132 were compared between freshly purified and in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells.
goal: to characterize cytokine receptor expression changes after expansion
key_materials: Antibodies for CD215, CD122, CD25, CD132

title: Phenotypic marker analysis of CD8+CD28− T cell subsets
description: Surface expression of markers related to differentiation, memory, immunomodulation, and cytotoxicity was analyzed on freshly isolated and expanded CD8+CD28− T cells.
goal: to define phenotypic heterogeneity and functional marker expression of CD8+CD28− T cells
key_materials: Antibodies for CD27, CD44, CCR7, PD-1, PD-L1, Tim-3, GITR, Granzyme B, Fas ligand

title: Grow Phaseolus vulgaris seedlings
description: Seeds of various Phaseolus vulgaris genotypes were sown in vermiculite and grown in a growth chamber at 23°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity. Seedlings were cultivated in plastic pots filled with moist vermiculite for 10–12 days until primary leaves were fully expanded.
goal: to grow seedlings to the fully-expanded primary leaf stage

title: Transplant seedlings and dark adaptation
description: Three seedlings were transplanted into moist vermiculite in 20 cm plastic pots and placed in a dark room 24 hours prior to inoculation.
goal: to prepare seedlings for inoculation by dark adaptation

title: Prepare viral vectors by cloning target gene fragments
description: Target gene fragments from P. vulgaris were amplified by PCR using specific primers and high fidelity polymerase. PCR products were digested with BamH1 and inserted into BamH1-digested and dephosphorylated pBPMV-IA-V1 plasmid to generate VIGS vectors. For BPMV-PvPDS-52 bp, a double-stranded synthetic oligonucleotide was directly cloned into the BamH1 site. Orientation of inserts was verified by PCR and sequencing.
goal: to construct BPMV-derived viral vectors for gene silencing

title: Prepare DNA-plasmid mix for primary inoculation
description: A 20 μL DNA-plasmid mix was prepared containing equal amounts of pBPMV-IA-R1M and either pBPMV-IA-V1 or pBPMV-GFP2 plasmids using 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer (mock buffer).
goal: to prepare inoculum for primary viral inoculation

title: Perform mechanical rub-inoculation of plants
description: Plants were placed in the dark 24 hours prior to inoculation. For primary inoculation, the DNA-plasmid mix was mechanically rubbed onto one primary leaf. For secondary inoculation, leaf sap from infected plants was prepared by grinding leaves in mock buffer and rubbed onto plants. Inoculated plants were grown at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle.
goal: to inoculate plants with BPMV constructs

title: Optimize rub-inoculation conditions
description: Different DNA plasmid amounts (1.5, 3, or 5 μg) and rubbing intensities (low, medium, high) were tested on P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine plants at the fully-expanded primary leaf stage to optimize inoculation efficiency.
goal: to optimize conditions for rub-inoculation of BPMV plasmids

title: Visualize GFP expression in plants
description: GFP expression in aerial organs and roots was examined using a UV lamp and photographed. Microscopic observations of roots were performed at 21 days post-inoculation using a microscope and camera.
goal: to detect and document GFP expression in inoculated plants

title: Analyze gene expression by semi-quantitative RT-PCR
description: Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed to cDNA. PCR amplification was performed using primers for PvPDS (outside silencing region) and PvUBI as internal control. PCR products were analyzed by agarose-ethidium bromide electrophoresis after 25 cycles.
goal: to assess gene expression levels post-silencing

title: Obtain Patient Blood Samples
description: Collected 166 blood samples from 41 patients admitted to Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong, between March and May 2003. Samples covered acute, convalescent, and recovered phases of SARS disease.

title: Test Patient Samples by RT-PCR
description: Tested samples from 7 patients for SARS-CoV by RT-PCR as described in a previous study, identifying 4 positive cases.

title: Culture Cell Lines
description: Cultured all cell lines in DMEM with Glutamax and high glucose, supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum and penicillin/streptomycin.
key_materials: Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) with Glutamax

title: Generate QT6/ACE2 Cell Line
description: Cloned human ACE2 gene from a human kidney cDNA library, subcloned into pcdna3.1+, transfected QT6 cells using lipofectamine 2000, and selected G418-resistant ACE2-positive cells.

title: Produce Viral Vectors
description: Transfected 293T cells with gag/pol, GFP reporter, and envelope constructs using Fugene-6. Harvested supernatant at 48 and 72 hours post-transfection, filtered, and stored at -80°C.

title: Measure Viral Vector Titer
description: Infected target cells with viral vectors and determined eGFP titers 72 hours later by FACS to quantify infectious units per milliliter.

title: Perform Live Virus Neutralization Assay
description: Heat-inactivated patient sera were serially diluted and incubated with 50 PFU SARS virus for 1 hour at 37°C. Vero E6 cells were added and incubated for 4 days. Neutralization was assessed by cytopathic effect.
goal: to assess neutralization of live SARS-CoV by patient sera

title: Perform Pseudotype Neutralization Assay
description: Heat-inactivated patient sera were 2-fold serially diluted and mixed with MLV(SARS) virions. After 1 hour incubation at 37°C, mixtures were added to QT6/ACE2 cells. GFP-positive cells were counted 48 hours later by fluorescence microscopy.
goal: to assess neutralization of SARS-CoV pseudotyped virus by patient sera

title: Analyze telomere dysfunction in stn1 mutants
description: Characterize growth defects and genome instability in stn1 mutants across generations by phenotypic classification and telomere length measurement.
goal: to describe the occurrence of telomere dysfunction phenotypes in stn1 mutants

title: Assess EXO1 effect on STN1-null telomeres
description: Analyze developmental defects, fertility, anaphase bridge frequency, and DNA damage response gene expression in exo1 stn1 mutants compared to stn1 mutants.
goal: to assess the effect of EXO1 on STN1-null telomeres

title: Measure telomere length and G-overhang size
description: Compare telomere length and G-overhang size between stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants to determine the role of EXO1 in telomere resection.
goal: to directly assay for telomere resection

title: Quantify telomeric permutation frequencies
description: Determine the frequency of telomeric terminal sequence permutations in stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants to assess EXO1-dependent sequence alterations.
goal: to examine whether the sequence alteration in STN1-depleted plants is caused by EXO1

title: Generate telomerase-null stn1 mutants
description: Create stn1 tert and exo1 stn1 tert mutants to study the contribution of telomerase to telomere maintenance and G-overhang extension.
goal: to test whether telomerase activity contributes to the elongated G-overhangs in stn1 mutants

title: Perform in gel hybridization for G-overhang quantification
description: Quantify G-overhang signals in telomerase-null and proficient stn1 and exo1 stn1 plants to evaluate telomerase's role in G-strand extension.
goal: to test whether telomerase activity contributes to the elongated G-overhangs in stn1 mutants

title: Analyze phenotypes of DNA polymerase α mutants
description: Characterize growth defects, developmental abnormalities, and genome instability in DNA polymerase α hypomorphic mutants.
goal: to test whether impairment of DNA polymerase α leads to phenotypes similar to STN1 depletion

title: Detect chromosome end-to-end fusions by fusion PCR
description: Identify and verify chromosome end-to-end fusions in pol α, icu2-1, and stn1 mutants by PCR and sequencing of subtelomeric regions.
goal: to determine whether anaphase bridges arise from chromosome-end-to-end fusions
key_materials: fusion PCR primers specific to subtelomeric regions

title: Analyze MCU and related protein mRNA levels
description: Collected and analyzed mRNA levels of MCU and related proteins (MCUb, MICU1-3, EMRE) from the TCGA breast cancer dataset to correlate expression with tumor size and lymph node infiltration.
goal: to decipher the role of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling in metastatic potential

title: Measure mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake after MCU silencing
description: Used siRNA to inhibit MCU in three TNBC cell lines and measured agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake using ATP or histamine as agonists.
goal: to verify the hypothesis that mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake is instrumental for metastasis

title: Assess cell motility via wound healing assay
description: Monitored cell motility in MCU-silenced TNBC cell lines using wound healing migration assay to evaluate the effect of MCU silencing on migration.
goal: to assess the impact of MCU silencing on cell motility

title: Measure cytosolic Ca2+ transients, SOCE, and ER Ca2+ content
description: Measured cytosolic Ca2+ transients, store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE), and ER Ca2+ content in MCU-silenced TNBC cell lines to determine effects on global Ca2+ signaling.
goal: to clarify whether migration impairment is due to reduced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake or other Ca2+ signaling changes

title: Overexpress MCU and measure mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake
description: Overexpressed MCU in TNBC cell lines and measured agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and cytosolic Ca2+ transients to assess mitochondrial buffering capacity.

title: Rescue MCU silencing with mouse MCU re-expression
description: Re-expressed mouse MCU in MCU-silenced MDA-MB-231 cells and assessed cell motility to confirm specificity of MCU silencing effects.

title: Perform in vitro spheroid invasion assay
description: Generated stable MCU-silenced cells, formed spheroids in agar, transferred them to collagen matrix, and monitored radial invasion to assess invasion potential.

title: Conduct colony formation assay
description: Performed colony formation assay over 7 days to evaluate the effect of MCU silencing on cell growth.

title: Stain planarian cells with Hoechst and MTG
description: Planarian cell suspension was stained with Hoechst 33342 to identify nuclear content and MTG to measure mitochondrial mass, allowing distinction of X1, X2, and Xins cell populations based on fluorescence signals.
goal: to measure mitochondrial mass differences among planarian cell populations

title: Test effect of Verapamil on MTG staining
description: Cells were treated with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, before MTG staining to determine if low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was due to dye efflux.
goal: to verify that low MTG fluorescence reflects true mitochondrial mass

title: Generate and characterize PIWI-1 antibody
description: An antibody against PIWI-1 was generated and characterized to identify neoblast populations by immunostaining, distinguishing PIWI-1 High, Low, and negative cells.

title: Immunostain planarian cells for PIWI-1
description: Planarian cells including X1, X2, and Xins populations were immunostained with PIWI-1 antibody to assess PIWI-1 protein levels and correlate with cell cycle phases.

title: Sort X1 cells into MTG High and Low populations
description: Within the X1 population, cells were sorted based on MTG fluorescence intensity into MTG High and MTG Low groups to investigate differences in pluripotency and PIWI-1 expression.

title: Perform RNA-seq on X1-MTG High and Low cells
description: Transcriptome sequencing was performed on sorted X1-MTG High and X1-MTG Low cells to identify differentially expressed genes and characterize neoblast heterogeneity.

title: Sort X2 cells by MTG signal and size (FSC)
description: X2 cells were sorted into MTG Low and High populations and further subdivided by forward scatter (FSC) into high and low size groups to analyze PIWI-1 expression and stem cell states.

title: Immunostain sorted X2-MTG populations for PIWI-1
description: Sorted X2-MTG Low and High cells (high and low FSC) were immunostained for PIWI-1 to determine the distribution of stem and progenitor cells within these populations.

title: Generate fluorescence reporter mice
description: Crossed Pax2-Cre mice with R26R-Lyn-Venus mice to produce fluorescence reporter mice for live-imaging analysis.
goal: to produce fluorescence reporter mice for live-imaging

title: Sacrifice mice at embryonic stages
description: Mice were sacrificed by cervical dislocation at embryonic day 15.5 or 16.5 to minimize suffering.

title: Immunostaining with primary antibodies
description: Used various primary antibodies at 1:200 dilution for immunostaining with appropriate fixatives (PFA or TCA) depending on the target epitope.

title: Whole-tissue immunofluorescence staining
description: Dissected epididymides were fixed, blocked, incubated with primary and secondary antibodies, and stained with phalloidin and Hoechst for visualization of F-actin and DNA.

title: Volumetric fluorescence imaging
description: Samples were mounted in agarose, optically cleared with BABB or CUBIC2, and imaged using confocal microscopy with various objective lenses.

title: Explant organ culture of epididymides
description: Epididymides with testis were dissected and cultured on inserts in medium at 37°C under 5% CO2 in an air-liquid interface.

title: Treatment with small-molecule inhibitors
description: Applied specific inhibitors to cultured samples to modulate cellular processes.

title: Live imaging of cultured epididymides
description: Prepared organ cultures with agarose to prevent sliding and performed live multiphoton imaging with specified parameters.

title: Scan maize CoREGs for acetyl-CoA-binding site
description: Each cloned HAG maize CoREG was scanned for the presence of an acetyl-CoA-binding site using the Conserved Domain Database. This region of approximately 75–90 amino acids was identified for further analysis.
goal: to identify acetyl-CoA-binding sites in maize CoREGs

title: Perform phylogenetic analysis of CoREG proteins
description: Related proteins were aligned using Clustal W with default parameters via the megalign program within the dnastar Lasergene package. For AUX/IAA CoREGs, full-length amino acid sequences were aligned using MUSCLE with specified parameters. Multiple sequence alignments were exported in Newick format and phylogenetic trees were displayed using FigTree.
goal: to perform phylogenetic analysis of maize CoREG proteins

title: Clone TF and CoREG ORFs into pENTR vectors
description: Targeted TF or CoREG open reading frames were amplified using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol. Optimization included addition of DMSO, MgCl2, or annealing temperature adjustments. Primers were designed without stop codons and with a 5′-CACC tail for directional cloning into pENTR vectors. Kanamycin-resistant colonies were screened by colony PCR or restriction digestion for correct inserts.
goal: to clone TF and CoREG ORFs into entry vectors

title: Confirm cloned inserts by Sanger sequencing
description: The sequence of cloned inserts was confirmed by single-read paired-end Sanger dideoxy sequencing. For clones longer than 1200 bp, internal primers were designed to complete sequence confirmation.
goal: to verify the sequence accuracy of cloned inserts

title: Clone ORFs into pENTR vectors
description: Targeted TF or CoREG ORFs were amplified using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with GC buffer and 10% glycerol. Primers were designed without stop codons and with a 5′-CACC tail for directional cloning into pENTR vectors. Kanamycin-resistant colonies were screened by colony PCR or restriction digestion, and inserts were sequence confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
goal: to clone targeted ORFs into pENTR vectors

title: Grow maize plants and isolate DNA/RNA
description: B73 maize plants were grown in a field nursery. Genomic DNA was isolated using a CTAB-based method. Total RNA was isolated from non-starchy tissues using RNAzol and from starchy tissues using a modified Li and Trick protocol. RNA integrity was verified by agarose gel electrophoresis with ethidium bromide staining.
goal: to isolate genomic DNA and total RNA from maize tissues

title: Test codon optimization of synthesized ORFs
description: Synthesized CDSs optimized for maize, yeast, or hybrid codon usage were recombined into GAL4-BD-GWC1 vector for yeast expression and into p1511 plasmid for GFP fusion under the 35S promoter to test expression in maize protoplasts.
goal: to determine codon optimization strategy for synthesized ORFs

title: Transform yeast and perform Western blot
description: Yeast cells were transformed with GAL4-BD-GWC1 constructs using the lithium acetate method. Cells were grown to OD600=0.6, lysed with NaOH, and proteins were prepared in SDS loading buffer. Proteins were separated by 10% SDS-PAGE and transferred to membrane. Membranes were blocked, incubated with primary and secondary antibodies, washed, and exposed to detect protein expression.
goal: to analyze protein expression of GAL4-BD fusion constructs in yeast
key_materials: secondary antibody (ECLTM Anti-mouse IgG Horseradish, NA931V)

title: Design probes from input sequences
description: Generate variable length probes (50-100 mers) at 5-bp steps from input sequences derived from gene models, full-length cDNA, and de novo assembled RNA-Seq contigs. Repeat-mask probes by removing those with high 15-mer frequency and eliminate probes with excessive matches to target sequences. Select unique probes at average 40 bp spacing to create the probe set.
goal: to design a unique probe set for array hybridization

title: Hybridize array with barley cultivars
description: Hybridize two slides of the array design with four barley cultivars using standard comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) protocols. Remove probes identified as repetitive elements or contaminants based on signal intensity and performance.
goal: to validate and optimize probe performance
key_materials: barley cultivars Steptoe, Barke, Morex, Bowman

title: Prepare Illumina TruSeq paired-end libraries
description: Fragment 1 μg genomic DNA to 200-300 bp using Covaris S220. Optionally size fractionate adapter-ligated products between 320-420 bp by gel excision. Purify libraries with AmPure XP beads and elute in resuspension buffer.
goal: to prepare sequencing libraries for capture
key_materials: Illumina TruSeq Paired End library kit

title: Perform pre-capture ligation-mediated PCR (LM-PCR)
description: Enrich correctly ligated DNA fragments by LM-PCR using Illumina adapters and Phusion polymerase. Quantify and analyze amplified libraries electrophoretically to confirm fragment size between 250-500 bp.
goal: to enrich and amplify sequencing libraries before capture

title: Prepare capture library with blocking oligos and enhancers
description: Add PCE and blocking oligos to amplified libraries, dry down the mixture, and pool up to six indexed samples proportionally. Add hybridization buffer components before denaturation and hybridization.
goal: to prepare libraries for sequence capture hybridization

title: Hybridize capture library to liquid array
description: Denature the prepared hybridization cocktail and incubate with liquid array in a thermocycler at 47°C for 64-72 hours to allow hybridization.
goal: to capture target sequences from libraries

title: Wash and purify captured DNA with Dynabeads
description: Prepare Dynabeads by washing and resuspension. Bind hybridization sample to beads at 47°C, wash sequentially with SC Wash Buffer I, Stringent Wash Buffer, and Wash Buffers I-III at specified temperatures and durations. Resuspend bead-bound captured library in PCR-grade water.
goal: to purify captured DNA from hybridization mixture

title: Amplify bead-bound captured library by LM-PCR
description: Perform LM-PCR amplification of bead-bound captured library with Illumina adapters and Phusion polymerase using specified cycling conditions. Combine reactions, purify with Qiaquick columns, and elute DNA. Assess purity and fragment size by spectrophotometry and Bioanalyzer.
goal: to enrich captured DNA for sequencing

title: Culture D. coniospora and extract genomic DNA
description: D. coniospora spores were cultured in liquid NGMY medium for 7 days. Mycelia were harvested by vacuum filtering, dried at 30°C, ground in liquid nitrogen, and DNA was extracted using the DNeasy Plant Mini Kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
goal: to extract fungal genomic DNA

title: Prepare samples and extract RNA from spores and mycelia
description: Fresh spores were inoculated in NGMY liquid medium and cultured either for 4 days or serially for 5 cycles of 8 days. Cultures were filtered, flash frozen, and stored at -80°C. Samples were homogenized in Trizol using a FastPrep-24, incubated on ice, homogenized again, and RNA was purified and cleaned with RNeasy mini Kit.
goal: to prepare RNA samples from spores and mycelia

title: Construct genomic DNA libraries and perform sequencing
description: MIseq paired-end libraries were prepared from genomic DNA and sequenced as 2 x 150 bp reads. For SOLiD sequencing, mate-paired libraries were prepared, DNA sheared to 1.5 kb or 3 kb fragments, nick-translated to <400 bp fragments, PCR amplified, size-selected (250-300 bp), purified, and converted for analysis with the 5500 WildFire system.
goal: to generate genomic DNA sequencing libraries and sequence them
key_materials: SOLiD Library Micro Column Purification Kit

title: Construct cDNA libraries and perform Illumina mRNA sequencing
description: cDNA libraries were constructed from mRNA of spores and mycelia and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000, generating over 48 million 90 bp paired-end reads per 200 bp insert library.
goal: to sequence mRNA from spores and mycelia

title: Perform de novo genome assembly
description: MIseq reads were filtered for quality and contaminants using BBDuk. Filtered reads were assembled de novo using Velvet, SPAdes, SOAPdenovo2, and ABySS with specified parameters. Resulting assemblies were scaffolded using high-quality SOLiD mate-paired reads with SSPACE v2.0.
goal: to assemble the D. coniospora genome de novo

title: Perform de novo transcriptome assembly
description: Combined reads from spores and mycelia mRNA sequencing libraries were assembled de novo into a transcriptome using Trinity with default parameters.
goal: to assemble the transcriptome de novo for gene prediction

title: Generate optical genome map
description: A whole genome map was generated using the Argus system with XbaI restriction enzyme selected for optimal fragment sizes. Molecules longer than 200 kb were assembled with MapSolver software, manually validated, resulting in 9 maps totaling 31.8 Mb for comparison with in silico digestion profiles.
goal: to generate a whole genome optical map for D. coniospora

title: Annotate genome for repetitive elements and non-coding RNA
description: Repetitive elements were identified using RepeatScout and masked with RepeatMasker. Transposable elements were characterized with TransposonPSI. Non-coding RNAs were identified using Rfam scan and tRNAscan-SE.
goal: to annotate repetitive elements and non-coding RNAs in the genome

title: siRNA Screen Setup and Infection
description: siRNA SMARTpools were dispensed into 384-well plates and stored at -80°C. On the day of transfection, plates were thawed, transfection reagent added, and complexes formed. Hela cells were trypsinised, counted, and added to wells. After 48 h incubation, cells were infected with HSV-1-eGFP virus or media. Virus replication was monitored by eGFP fluorescence from 24 to 80 h post-infection.
goal: to perform siRNA knockdown and measure HSV-1 replication

title: Cell Viability Assay Using CellTiter Blue
description: Following siRNA transfection, CellTiter Blue reagent was added to wells. Plates were incubated for 2 h at 37°C before fluorescence measurement. Readings were normalized to mock-transfected cells to assess cytotoxicity of siRNAs.
goal: to determine cytotoxicity of siRNAs

title: Yeast Two-Hybrid Protein Interaction Screen
description: HSV-1 clones were cloned into bait vectors and screened against a prey library using a semi-automated yeast two-hybrid assay. Interacting prey cDNAs were identified by database blasting. High-confidence interactions were selected based on repeated isolation or related prey interactions.
goal: to identify protein-protein interactions between HSV-1 and human proteins

title: Bioinformatic Analysis of Protein Interactions
description: HSV-1-human protein interactions were integrated with human protein interaction networks from multiple databases. Betweenness centrality was calculated and functional enrichment analyses performed. Known protein complexes were analyzed for consistent effects using statistical tests.
goal: to analyze and interpret protein interaction networks

title: siRNA SMARTpool Deconvolution for Validation
description: Four individual siRNAs per gene and reconstituted SMARTpools were diluted and dispensed into plates. Transfection and infection were performed as in the primary screen. Replication slopes were calculated and phenotypes validated if two or more siRNAs showed consistent effects.
goal: to validate siRNA knockdown effects on HSV-1 replication

title: HSV-1 Replication Assay in 96-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were diluted and dispensed into 96-well plates. Dharmafect 1 was added and complexes formed. Hela cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with HSV-1. Virus replication was monitored by eGFP fluorescence from 24 to 80 h post-infection.
goal: to measure HSV-1 replication after siRNA treatment

title: VZV Replication Assay in 384-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were diluted and dispensed into 384-well plates. Dharmafect 1 was added and complexes formed. MeWo cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with VZV-eGFP-infected MeWo cells. Virus growth was measured by eGFP fluorescence at 3 h intervals from 44 to 72 h post-infection.
goal: to measure VZV replication after siRNA treatment

title: hCMV Replication Assay in 384-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were diluted and dispensed into 384-well plates. Dharmafect 1 was added and complexes formed. MRC-5 cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with hCMV-GFP. Virus replication was monitored by eGFP fluorescence from 24 to 80 h post-infection.
goal: to measure hCMV replication after siRNA treatment

title: Confirm viral vector infectivity on embryos
description: Microinject AAV, adenoviral, and lentiviral vectors encoding EGFP into the perivitelline space of pronuclear-stage mouse embryos and confirm EGFP expression at morula/blastocyst stage by fluorescence microscopy.
goal: to confirm infectivity of viral vectors on embryos

title: Co-culture embryos with viral vectors
description: Co-culture embryos with intact zona pellucida with viral vectors and observe infection efficiency by transgene expression.
goal: to test infection efficiency of viral vectors on embryos with intact zona pellucida

title: Test AAV vector infection on parthenogenetic embryos
description: Infect parthenogenetic embryos with AAV vector and confirm infection by transgene expression.
goal: to test if AAV vector can pass through intact zona pellucida

title: Evaluate AAV transduction efficiency in rat and bovine embryos
description: Infect rat and bovine embryos with AAV6 vector and assess transduction efficiency.
goal: to evaluate AAV vector suitability for donor DNA delivery across mammalian species

title: Knockin at mouse Rosa26 locus using scAAV vector
description: Introduce Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage mouse embryos by electroporation, infect with scAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by Rosa26 homology arms, and assess knockin efficiency at blastocyst stage and in offspring.
goal: to deliver donor DNA for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockin in mouse embryos

title: Knockin at mouse Rosa26 locus using ssAAV vector
description: Perform knockin in mouse embryos using ssAAV vector with longer Rosa26 homology arms and assess knockin efficiency and germline transmission.
goal: to deliver donor DNA for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockin in mouse embryos

title: Knockin at rat Rosa26 locus using scAAV vector
description: Introduce Cas9-RNP into rat embryos by electroporation, infect with scAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by Rosa26 homology arms, and evaluate knockin efficiency and germline transmission.
goal: to deliver donor DNA for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockin in rat embryos

title: Knockin at rat Rosa26 locus using ssAAV vector
description: Perform knockin in rat embryos using ssAAV vector with longer Rosa26 homology arms and assess knockin efficiency, mosaicism, and germline transmission.
goal: to deliver donor DNA for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockin in rat embryos

title: Cell culture of various cell lines
description: Cultured 293T, 293L, iSLK.219, TRExBCBL1-RTA, and BCBL-1 cells in appropriate media supplemented with serum, antibiotics, and selection agents. Induced iSLK.219 cells with recombinant KSHV BACs using doxycycline.
goal: to maintain and propagate cell lines under selective conditions

title: Generation of lentiviral vectors and transduction
description: Generated lentiviral vectors by cloning genes into vectors and transfecting 293T cells with packaging vectors to produce virions. Collected viruses were used to transduce target cells followed by puromycin selection to obtain pure populations.
goal: to generate stable cell lines expressing ORF59-Flag or dsRed-ORF59-Flag

title: Transfection of BAC16 ORF59-Flag into 293L cells
description: Transfected BAC16 ORF59-Flag into 293L cells using Metafectene Pro reagent followed by hygromycin selection to obtain cells maintaining KSHV BACs.
goal: to establish 293L cells harboring BAC16 ORF59-Flag

title: Plasmid construction and cloning
description: Generated plasmids by PCR amplification and cloning of target genes and their truncations into respective vectors. Confirmed clone integrity by sequencing.

title: Generation of Flag-tagged ORF59 BACmid by homologous recombination
description: Inserted Flag epitope tag at C-terminus of ORF59 in BAC16 by two-step seamless galK positive/counter selection homologous recombination. Selected mutants on antibiotic plates and confirmed by restriction digestion, Southern blot, PCR, and sequencing.
goal: to generate recombinant KSHV BAC16 with ORF59-Flag tag

title: Co-immunoprecipitation and Western blotting
description: Transfected 293T cells with expression vectors using PEI. Lysed cells in RIPA buffer with protease inhibitors, precleared lysates, and immunoprecipitated proteins with specific antibodies. Washed beads, boiled samples, ran SDS-PAGE, transferred to membranes, and detected proteins by Western blot using infrared imaging.

title: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)
description: Cross-linked cells with formaldehyde, quenched with glycine, lysed cells, isolated nuclei, and sonicated chromatin. Precleared chromatin and immunoprecipitated with antibodies overnight. Washed beads, eluted chromatin, reversed cross-links, treated with proteinase K, purified DNA, and used for qPCR.
key_materials: salmon sperm DNA-protein A-protein G Sepharose slurry

title: Low-cell chromatin immunoprecipitation assay
description: Fixed 1 million cells, washed, resuspended in chromatin-shearing buffer, sonicated chromatin to ~500 bp, and immunoprecipitated chromatin with specific antibodies as per kit instructions.

title: Antibody selection for ChIP
description: Selection and use of specific antibodies for chromatin immunoprecipitation targeting histone modifications H3K4Me3, H3K9Me3, H3K27Me3, and total H3.

title: Fixation and sorting of Drosophila larval brain cells
description: Dissection of larval brains 48 hours after hatching, fixation with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, quenching with glycine, dissociation of brains, and sorting of cells by GFP strength and size to isolate type II neural stem cells.
goal: to fix and isolate pure populations of type II neural stem cells from Drosophila larval brains

title: Fixation and sorting of K562 cells
description: Culture of K562 cells at 37°C with 5% CO2, fixation with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, quenching with glycine, staining with Hoechst, and sorting 100 cells directly into RIPA buffer.
goal: to fix and sort K562 cells for downstream analysis
key_materials: RPMI medium with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum

title: Culture and Fix K562 Cells
description: K562 cells were cultured in RPMI medium supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum at 37°C and 5% CO2. Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, quenched with 125 mM glycine, and sorted using Hoechst stain on a BD FACSAria cell sorter. A total of 100 cells were sorted directly into RIPA 140 mM buffer.

title: Conventional ChIP-Seq Sample Preparation
description: Fixed cells were resuspended in 140 mM RIPA buffer and sonicated for 14 cycles using a bioruptor. After centrifugation, the supernatant was incubated overnight with 2 μg of specific antibody at 4°C. Protein A and G Dynabeads were added to capture antibodies, followed by sequential washes with RIPA buffers and TE buffer. Samples were treated with RNase and Proteinase K to reverse cross-links, then DNA was extracted by phenol–chloroform and dissolved in TE buffer. DNA was converted into sequencing libraries using the NebNext Ultra II kit.
goal: to prepare chromatin immunoprecipitation samples for sequencing
key_materials: NebNext Ultra II DNA library preparation kit

title: TAF-ChIP Sample Preparation and Library Construction
description: Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde and quenched with glycine, washed with PBS, and sorted into RIPA buffer. Nuclei were sonicated at low power to fragment chromatin. Protein A and G Dynabeads were coupled with antibody in blocking buffer. Chromatin was incubated overnight with antibody-coupled beads. Beads were washed with tagmentation buffer and subjected to tagmentation using Nextera enzyme. After tagmentation, beads were washed with RIPA and TE buffers. Samples underwent Proteinase K treatment overnight at 60°C. DNA was either phenol–chloroform extracted and precipitated or directly PCR-amplified after heat inactivation of Proteinase K. PCR products were purified by bead-based size selection, analyzed for size and concentration, pooled, and sequenced.
goal: to perform TAF-ChIP and prepare sequencing libraries
key_materials: blocking buffer (RIPA + BSA + glycogen + yeast tRNA)

title: PCR purification by bead-based size selection
description: Ampure Xp beads were added to the PCR reaction at 0.2× ratio to bind and remove fragments larger than 1,000 bp. The magnetic beads were separated using a magnetic rack and the supernatant was transferred to a fresh tube. Then, Ampure Xp beads were added at 0.8× ratio to bind the target library.
goal: to purify PCR reaction by removing large fragments and isolating target library

title: Library size and concentration analysis
description: After PCR purification, the libraries were analyzed on an Agilent Bioanalyzer to assess size distribution and measured for concentration using a Qubit fluorometer.
goal: to analyze library size distribution and measure concentration

title: Screen Arabidopsis genes for Chl metabolism regulators
description: Screened publicly available datasets for Arabidopsis genes of unknown function exhibiting transcriptional signatures of chlorophyll biosynthesis and catabolism genes, identifying At2g35260 (BCM1).
goal: to identify novel regulators of chlorophyll biosynthesis and catabolism

title: Immunoblot analysis of BCM1 protein accumulation
description: Performed immunoblot analyses using BCM1 antiserum to detect BCM1 protein accumulation in various Arabidopsis tissues and developmental stages.
goal: to determine BCM1 protein accumulation patterns

title: Subcellular localization of BCM1
description: Used transient expression of BCM1-YFP in Arabidopsis protoplasts and immunoblot analyses of chloroplast subfractions to localize BCM1 mainly to the thylakoid membrane, especially stroma lamellae.
goal: to determine BCM1 subcellular localization

title: Determine BCM1 membrane association type
description: Treated isolated thylakoids with reagents to test whether BCM1 is an integral or peripheral membrane protein, finding BCM1 behaves as an integral membrane protein.
goal: to clarify BCM1 membrane association

title: Phenotypic characterization of bcm1 mutants and BCM1 overexpressors
description: Characterized chlorophyll biosynthesis status in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX plants, observing pale-green phenotypes in mutants and increased ALA synthesis in overexpressors.
goal: to investigate BCM1 function in chlorophyll biosynthesis

title: Measure ALA synthesis and chlorophyll intermediates
description: Measured ALA synthesis rates and levels of Proto, Mg-porphyrins, chlorophyll, and heme in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX seedlings to assess effects on tetrapyrrole biosynthesis.
goal: to assess BCM1 impact on chlorophyll biosynthesis intermediates

title: Analyze expression of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes and proteins
description: Examined transcript levels of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes by qRT-PCR and protein levels of key enzymes by immunoblot in bcm1 and BCM1-OX seedlings.
goal: to determine BCM1 effect on gene and protein expression

title: Genetic interaction analysis of bcm1 with gun5 and gun4 mutants
description: Generated double mutants combining bcm1-3 with gun5-1 and gun4 alleles to study genetic interactions affecting chlorophyll biosynthesis and Mg chelation.
goal: to investigate genetic interactions between BCM1 and Mg chelatase components

title: Mouse strain preparation and genotyping
description: Various mouse strains including C57BL/6, Tlr7−/−, Tlr9−/−, and Myd88−/− were used. Double knockout mice (Tlr7−/− Tlr9−/−) were bred in house. All strains were confirmed to have a C57BL/6 background greater than 95% by microsatellite genotyping.

title: Parasite preparation and infection
description: P. berghei ANKA parasites were maintained in C57BL/6 mice. Blood was harvested by cardiac puncture from infected mice on day 5 post-infection. 10^6 infected erythrocytes were injected intraperitoneally into new mice in 100 μl of Alsever’s solution. Infections were initiated at 14:00 hours.
goal: to infect mice with P. berghei parasites

title: Blood collection for cytokine analysis
description: Blood was collected from infected mice by submandibular blood collection or cardiac puncture into K2EDTA tubes for plasma isolation used in cytokine analysis.

title: Monitoring infection and cerebral malaria symptoms
description: Survival and signs of cerebral malaria were monitored daily, and twice daily during peak lethality (days 6-12). Parasitaemia was monitored daily by Giemsa-stained thin blood smears. Animals showing neurological symptoms or dying by day 12 post-infection were considered to have cerebral malaria.

title: Statistical analysis of parasitaemia and survival
description: Parasitaemia data were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test (α=0.05). Survival data were analyzed by comparing Kaplan-Meier curves using the log rank (Mantel-Cox) test (α=0.05).

title: Plasma cytokine measurement
description: Plasma cytokines were measured using a multiplexed cytometric bead immunoassay according to manufacturer instructions and detected on a MAGPIX instrument. Cytokine levels were statistically assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test (α=0.05).

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Muscle Extracts
description: Satellite cells associated with myofibers were treated with TA muscle extracts in floating culture conditions to examine activation markers such as PAX7, MYOD, Ki67, and EdU incorporation.
goal: to examine the effect of muscle extracts on satellite cell activation

title: Co-culture Intact and Damaged Myofibers
description: Healthy intact myofibers were co-cultured with mechanically damaged myofibers to assess whether damaged myofiber-derived factors (DMDFs) stimulate activation and proliferation of satellite cells on intact myofibers.
goal: to evaluate satellite cell activation by DMDFs excluding non-muscle cell factors

title: Washout and Recovery of Satellite Cells
description: After co-culture with damaged myofibers, the damaged myofibers and media containing DMDFs were washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM to observe if activated satellite cells revert to a quiescent-like state.
goal: to test whether activated satellite cells in G1 phase return to quiescence

title: Proteome Analysis of Myofiber Supernatants
description: Proteins ranging from 10 to 50 kDa were analyzed by proteome analysis to identify candidate DMDFs differentially present in supernatants from intact versus damaged myofibers.
goal: to identify DMDFs that stimulate satellite cell activation
key_materials: protein samples from intact and damaged myofiber supernatants

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Recombinant Metabolic Enzymes
description: Isolated myofibers with satellite cells were treated with recombinant metabolic enzymes or controls in floating culture for 72 hours, followed by immunostaining for activation markers MYOD and PAX7.
goal: to test if extracellular metabolic enzymes stimulate satellite cell activation

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Metabolic Enzymes in Non-Glucose Medium
description: Satellite cells were treated with metabolic enzymes in a glucose-free medium to determine if activation occurs independently of glucose metabolism.
goal: to exclude glucose metabolism as a cause of satellite cell activation by metabolic enzymes

title: Test c-MET Inhibitor Effect on DMDF-Induced Activation
description: The c-MET inhibitor PHA-665752 was applied to satellite cells treated with recombinant DMDFs to assess whether HGF/c-MET signaling is required for DMDF-induced activation.
goal: to determine if HGF signaling is necessary for DMDF-induced satellite cell activation

title: Mechanically Damage Myofibers
description: Freshly isolated healthy intact myofibers were mechanically damaged using a Pasteur pipette in culture dishes. Damage was confirmed by observing shrunken morphology.
goal: to obtain mechanically damaged myofibers for co-culture experiments

title: Ethical approval and tissue micro-dissection
description: Ethical approval was obtained. Laser micro-dissection (LMD) was performed on formalin-fixed/paraffin-embedded tissue using a Zeiss/PALM Microscope. SMA staining was performed using a mouse monoclonal antibody and an automated stainer under standard conditions.
goal: to obtain and prepare specific fibroblast populations from tissue samples

title: Cell culture and genetic modification
description: MCF7 and HB2 cells were cultured. Stable GFP expression was introduced using pTH-GFPa vector. MCF7 cells expressing firefly luciferase were obtained. Primary fibroblasts were isolated and immortalized by hTERT retroviral transduction. Reverse transfection of pre-/anti-miR and plasmids was performed using HiPerFect. Stable miR-26b knockdown was achieved using pmiRZIP lentiviral vectors.
goal: to culture and genetically modify cells for functional assays

title: Functional cell assays
description: Assays for cell viability, cell cycle, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were performed. Flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting were conducted. Spheroid invasion assays were performed with formalin-fixed/paraffin-embedded spheroids sectioned and stained with haematoxylin/eosin or immunohistochemistry using anti-cytokeratin antibody. Dual luciferase assays were conducted using pmiRGLO reporter.
goal: to assess cellular functions and invasion capabilities

title: RNA extraction and gene expression analysis
description: RNA was extracted from FFPE tissue using RecoverAll kit. miRNA and mRNA were extracted from cell lines using MirVana and RNeasy kits, respectively. qPCR analyses were performed in triplicate using Taqman assays. Microarray analyses of miRNA expression were performed using Agilent human miRNA arrays.
goal: to extract RNA and analyze gene and miRNA expression
key_materials: RecoverAll Total Nucleic Acid Isolation kit (Ambion)
human miRNA v2 arrays and system v1.7 reagents (Agilent)

title: Protein mass spectrometry analysis
description: Peptides from processed cell pellet lysates were separated by capillary liquid chromatography and analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry using RSLCnano and LTQ-Orbitrap Velos instruments. Data were searched against the IPI Human database and label-free quantitation was performed using MaxQuant software.
goal: to identify and quantify proteins in cell lysates

title: Statistical data analysis
description: Statistical analyses were performed using Prism with two-tailed tests. Mass spectrometry data were analyzed using R; expression levels were log2 median-normalized, analyzed with t-tests, and p-values adjusted to false discovery rates using Benjamini–Hochberg method.
goal: to analyze experimental data statistically

title: Compile TDP43 homolog sequence database
description: Collected protein sequences of 93 vertebrate TDP43 homologs and separated them into NTDs, RRM domains, and CTDs for evolutionary sequence analysis.
goal: to decode the rules relating TDP43 phase behavior to amino-acid sequence

title: Calculate sequence diversity by edit distance
description: Calculated the Levenshtein (edit) distance normalized to 100 amino acids between all members of NTD, RRM, and CTD collections to assess sequence diversity.
goal: to measure sequence diversity within TDP43 domain collections

title: Analyze amino-acid composition of TDP43 CTD subdomains
description: Analyzed amino-acid composition of the conserved region (CR) and two intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) flanking the CR to identify compositional biases and residue enrichment.
goal: to identify conserved sequence patterns in TDP43 CTD

title: Assess hydrophobic residue spacing in TDP43 IDRs
description: Examined the number, relative position, and spacing of hydrophobic residues in IDRs and calculated hydrophobicity using sliding windows and multiple hydrophobicity scales.
goal: to characterize conserved hydrophobic patterns in TDP43 IDRs

title: Generate TDP43RRM-GFP phase separation reporter
description: Replaced RNA-binding RRM domains of TDP43 with GFP to create a reporter protein that forms micron-sized liquid droplets for live-cell phase separation analysis.
goal: to rapidly measure TDP43 LLPS in living cells

title: Mutate TDP43 CTD hydrophobic residues to serine
description: Created mutants by substituting all hydrophobic residues (VLIMFYW) in the CTD with serine to test their role in phase separation and localization.
goal: to assess the role of hydrophobic residues in TDP43 phase separation

title: Quantify nuclear and total GFP fluorescence by microscopy and flow cytometry
description: Measured nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in thousands of cells expressing WT or mutant TDP43RRM-GFP to estimate saturation concentration (Csat) for phase separation.
goal: to estimate changes in phase separation threshold caused by mutations

title: Mutate aromatic and aliphatic residues separately
description: Generated mutants substituting all phenylalanine residues to serine (F-S), all aromatic residues to serine (FYW-S), and all aliphatic residues to serine (VLIM-S) to dissect their contributions to phase separation.
goal: to parse roles of aromatic versus aliphatic residues in phase separation

title: Design and clone cDNAs into pBABED-Puro vectors
description: cDNAs encoding various FLAG-tagged proteins and human VHL were designed from published protein sequences and cloned into pBABED-Puro vectors for constitutive expression.
goal: to generate plasmids for constitutive expression of target proteins

title: Verify DNA constructs by sequencing
description: All DNA constructs were verified by DNA sequencing performed by the DNA Sequencing and Services facility using Big-Dye chemistry on an automated capillary DNA sequencer.
goal: to confirm the accuracy of cloned DNA sequences
key_materials: Applied Biosystems model 3730 automated capillary DNA sequencer

title: Obtain retroviral expression system vectors
description: Retroviral expression system vectors pCMV-Gag-Pol and pCMV-VSVG were obtained from Clontech, as well as pRetroX-Tet-On and pRetroX-Tight vectors for inducible AdPROM expression.

title: Obtain siRNAs for gene silencing
description: Non-targeting control siRNAs and SHP2 siRNA pool were obtained from Dharmacon for use in gene silencing experiments.

title: Culture human and mouse cell lines
description: Human U2OS, A549, MDA-MB-468, MDA-MB-231, K-562 cells and mouse J774 monocyte cells were cultured in DMEM or RPMI supplemented with FBS, l-glutamine, and penicillin/streptomycin at 37°C with 5% CO2.

title: Produce retroviruses by co-transfection in 293-FT cells
description: pBABED retroviral plasmids were co-transfected with pCMV-gag-pol and pCMV-VSV-G into 293-FT cells using PEI in Opti-MEM medium. After incubation, medium was replaced and retroviruses collected and filtered.
goal: to generate retroviral particles for infection

title: Infect target cells with retroviral medium and select
description: Target cells at ~60% confluency were infected with retroviral medium containing polybrene for 24 h, then selected with puromycin to enrich for cells with integrated retrovirus.
goal: to establish stable cell lines expressing target proteins

title: Lyse cells and prepare protein extracts
description: Cells were washed with PBS, scraped in lysis buffer supplemented with protease inhibitors and β-mercaptoethanol, then clarified. Extracts were processed immediately or snap-frozen for storage.
key_materials: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl pH 7.5, 0.27 M sucrose, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM sodium orthovanadate, 10 mM sodium β-glycerophosphate, 50 mM sodium fluoride, 5 mM sodium pyrophosphate, 1% Nonidet P-40)

title: Isolate mRNAs from adult Drosophila heads
description: mRNAs were isolated from adult heads of TBPH-null alleles and wild-type flies to analyze gene expression differences.
goal: to identify molecules involved in neurodegeneration caused by TBPH absence

title: Hybridize mRNAs to GeneChip Drosophila Genome Arrays
description: Isolated mRNAs were hybridized to microarrays to detect differences in gene expression patterns between TBPH-null and wild-type flies.
goal: to analyze gene expression differences related to TBPH function

title: Confirm retrotransposon upregulation by qRT-PCR
description: Quantitative RT-PCR was used to validate the upregulation of retrotransposons detected by microarray in TBPH-null fly heads.
goal: to confirm increased retrotransposon activity in TBPH mutants
key_materials: qRT-PCR primers targeting retrotransposon RNA sequences

title: Detect gypsy env glycoprotein expression
description: Expression of the gypsy-encoded env glycoprotein was measured to confirm retrotransposon activation in TBPH-null heads.
goal: to verify increased gypsy retrotransposon activity
key_materials: antibodies or detection reagents for gypsy env protein

title: Genetically rescue retrotransposon activation by TBPH expression
description: Expression of TBPH protein in mutant flies was used to repress activation of accord and gypsy retrotransposons.
goal: to demonstrate TBPH's specific role in retrotransposon repression

title: Treat TBPH-null flies with reverse transcriptase inhibitors
description: Oral administration of nucleoside and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors was performed to assess effects on locomotive defects in TBPH-null larvae.
goal: to test if retrotransposon activation contributes to TBPH-null phenotypes

title: Silence gypsy retrotransposon using RNAi in neurons
description: Neuronal expression of RNAi against gypsy was used to reduce its expression and assess rescue of locomotive and synaptic defects in TBPH-null larvae.
goal: to test the role of gypsy in TBPH-null neurodegeneration

title: Silence gypsy retrotransposon in glial cells
description: Glial-specific RNAi against gypsy was expressed to evaluate effects on locomotive phenotypes in TBPH-null flies.
goal: to determine if glial gypsy repression rescues TBPH-null defects

title: Animal preparation and stereotaxic surgery
description: Male albino Wistar rats were anesthetized with chloral hydrate and positioned in a stereotaxic apparatus. Injections of vehicle, LPS, or LPS plus RU486 were made into the substantia nigra (SN) at specified coordinates relative to bregma. Different groups received different treatments and stress protocols.
goal: to administer treatments into the substantia nigra of rats under anesthesia

title: Chronic variate stress model application
description: A 9-day variate stressor paradigm was applied to stressed groups, including restraint stress and forced swimming at varying times to minimize predictability. Nonstressed animals were kept undisturbed. Body weight was measured before and after treatment as an indirect HPA axis activation parameter.
goal: to induce chronic variate stress in rats

title: Serum corticosterone measurement
description: Blood was collected from the heart of deeply anesthetized rats. Serum corticosterone concentration was measured using an ELISA kit following the manufacturer's instructions.
goal: to measure serum corticosterone levels
key_materials: enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit (Assay Designs Correlate-EIA)

title: Immunohistological evaluation of brain sections
description: Coronal brain sections were cut and mounted. Sections were treated with hydrogen peroxide, blocked with serum, incubated with primary antibodies, then with biotinylated secondary antibodies, followed by ExtrAvidin–Peroxidase. Peroxidase activity was visualized by diaminobenzidine–hydrogen peroxide reaction.
goal: to detect specific proteins in brain tissue by immunohistochemistry

title: Immunohistochemical data analysis
description: Immunohistochemical staining was analyzed in a defined region of the substantia nigra. Areas lacking GFAP immunoreactivity were measured, OX-6-positive cells were counted using a grid and unbiased counting frames, and TH-positive neurons were estimated using a fractionator sampling design.
goal: to quantify immunohistochemical markers in brain sections

title: Immunofluorescence double-labelling
description: Brain sections were blocked with serum, incubated overnight with primary antibodies for double-labelling, then incubated with fluorescent secondary antibodies. Nuclei were counterstained with Hoechst dye. Controls were performed to verify specificity. Fluorescence images were acquired by confocal microscopy.
goal: to visualize co-localization of proteins by immunofluorescence
key_materials: secondary antibodies conjugated to fluorescein or Alexa Fluor 594

title: Real-time RT-PCR analysis
description: The left substantia nigra was dissected, snap-frozen, and total RNA extracted. cDNA was synthesized from RNA. Real-time PCR was performed using SYBR Green chemistry with specific primers. Amplification conditions and melting curve analysis were conducted to confirm product specificity. β-actin was used as a reference gene.
goal: to quantify gene expression levels by real-time RT-PCR
key_materials: primers for TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, iNOS, CD200, CX3CR1, MCP-1, β-actin

title: Chronic variate stress application
description: A 9-day variate stressor paradigm was applied to stressed groups, including restraint in a plastic tube and forced swimming in water at controlled temperature. Stressors were applied at varying times to minimize predictability. Body weight was measured before and after treatment as an indirect HPA axis activation parameter.
goal: to induce chronic variate stress in rats

title: Obtain Arabidopsis accessions
description: Arabidopsis accessions used in the study were obtained from the Nottingham Arabidopsis Stock Centre and other sources.

title: Generate HaRxL62 expression construct
description: The ORF of HaRxL62 from the signal peptide cleavage site was cloned into pENTR/SD/D-TOPO and recombined into the Gateway destination binary vector pENS-StrepII-3×HA-GW under the control of the Cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoter.
goal: to generate a construct for expressing HaRxL62 in planta

title: Transform Arabidopsis with HaRxL62 construct
description: The HaRxL62 construct was transferred into Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain GV3101 and transformed into Arabidopsis Col-0 by floral dipping. Primary transformants were selected on BASTA-containing soil and expression was confirmed by Western blot.
goal: to transform Arabidopsis with HaRxL62 construct

title: Select homozygous transgenic Arabidopsis lines
description: Progeny of T2 generation were observed for 3:1 BASTA resistance segregation. Homozygous lines were selected by examining BASTA resistance in T3 seedlings. Two independent transgenic lines were analyzed.

title: Grow Arabidopsis for Hpa inoculation assay
description: Arabidopsis plants were grown at 22°C and 60% humidity under a 10-hour photoperiod and 14-hour dark period in controlled growth cabinets for Hpa inoculation assays.

title: Grow Arabidopsis for SA-induced PR1 expression
description: Arabidopsis plants were grown on 0.7% agar plates of MS medium at 22°C under a 16-hour photoperiod and 8-hour dark period in controlled growth cabinets for SA-induced PR1 expression analysis.

title: Generate HaRxL62 Transgenic Arabidopsis Lines
description: The HaRxL62 ORF was cloned into a Gateway binary vector under the 35S promoter, transformed into Agrobacterium, and then introduced into Arabidopsis Col-0 by floral dipping. Primary transformants were selected on BASTA-containing soil and confirmed by Western blot. Homozygous lines were selected from T3 seedlings based on BASTA resistance.
goal: to generate Arabidopsis lines expressing HaRxL62

title: Perform Hpa Infection on Arabidopsis
description: Arabidopsis plants were spray-inoculated to saturation with a spore suspension of Hpa and covered with a transparent lid to maintain high humidity (90–100%) at 16°C under a 10-hour photoperiod until sampling.

title: Intranasal and Subcutaneous Vaccination with VRP-SARS-N
description: BALB/c mice were vaccinated twice at 6–7 week intervals with VRP-SARS-N or control VRP-GFP via intranasal (i.n.) or subcutaneous (s.c.) routes prior to SARS-CoV challenge to evaluate differences in protection and T cell responses.
goal: to evaluate protection and T cell responses induced by different vaccination routes

title: Depletion of Memory CD4+ T Cells Prior to Challenge
description: Memory CD4+ T cells were depleted systemically 2 days or 98 days prior to SARS-CoV challenge to assess their role in protection and recovery of CD4+ T cells.
goal: to determine the importance of memory CD4+ T cells in protection

title: Localization of CD4+ T Cells by Dual Antibody Labeling
description: Cells were simultaneously labeled by intravenous (i.v.) and intranasal (i.n.) administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies respectively, 5–7 weeks after boosting to distinguish airway, parenchymal, and vascular CD4+ T cell populations.
goal: to discriminate anatomical localization of CD4+ T cells in respiratory tract

title: Phenotypic and Functional Analysis of Airway CD4+ T Cells
description: Surface markers and cytokine production (IFN-γ, TNF, IL-10, IL-2) of airway, parenchymal, and vascular N353-specific CD4+ T cells were analyzed to assess phenotype and effector function.
goal: to characterize phenotype and effector function of airway memory CD4+ T cells
key_materials: Flow cytometry antibodies for CD127, CD27, CD11a, CD69, CD103, Ly6C

title: FTY720 and BrdU Treatment to Assess T Cell Proliferation and Recruitment
description: Infected mice were treated with FTY720 to block T cell egress from lymphoid tissue and with BrdU for 4 hours to determine the contribution of local proliferation versus recruitment to airway N353 CD4+ T cell numbers.
goal: to determine mechanisms maintaining airway memory CD4+ T cells

title: Intranasal Depletion of Airway CD4+ T Cells
description: Airway CD4+ T cells were selectively depleted by intranasal administration of anti-CD4+ antibody prior to SARS-CoV challenge to assess their role in protection and survival.
goal: to evaluate the protective role of airway CD4+ T cells

title: Measurement of IFN-γ and Other Cytokine Expression Post Vaccination
description: IFN-γ mRNA and protein expression in lungs and airway CD4+ T cells were measured after vaccination and challenge using mRNA analysis and in vivo cytokine expression assay with Brefeldin A treatment.
goal: to assess IFN-γ production by airway CD4+ T cells

title: Neutralization of IFN-γ in Airways
description: IFN-γ was neutralized in the airway by intranasal administration of antibody prior to infection and every 2 days thereafter to evaluate effects on gene expression, survival, pathology, and virus clearance.
goal: to determine the role of airway IFN-γ in protection

title: Maintain and synchronize C. elegans strains
description: Animals were maintained at 25°C using standard culture conditions and synchronized through alkaline hypochlorite treatment of gravid adults to isolate eggs.
goal: to maintain and synchronize C. elegans populations

title: Construct repair template using SapTrap
description: SapTrap was used to assemble a 30xlinker::GFP^SEC^TEV::AID degron::3xFLAG repair template (pJW1747) for knock-in into the 3′ end of the nhr-25 gene using various plasmids and PCR products in DH10β competent E. coli cells.
goal: to generate a repair template for gene knock-in

title: Purify repair template plasmid
description: The pJW1747 repair template plasmid was purified using the Invitrogen PureLink HQ Mini Plasmid DNA Purification Kit with an optional wash step using 4 M guanidine-HCl and 40% isopropanol to improve injection efficiency.
goal: to purify plasmid DNA for microinjection
key_materials: Invitrogen PureLink HQ Mini Plasmid DNA Purification Kit

title: Microinject N2 animals with plasmid mix
description: N2 animals were injected with a mix of pJW1747, pDD121, and co-injection markers to generate knock-ins as previously described.
goal: to create gene knock-in animals

title: Verify knock-in junctions by PCR
description: Knock-in junctions were verified by PCR using primers binding outside the homology arm paired with primers within pJW1747.
goal: to confirm successful gene knock-in

title: Backcross and excise SEC cassette
description: Knock-in animals were backcrossed five times to wild-type N2 and the SEC cassette was excised by heat-shock to produce final strains, confirmed by PCR and sequencing.
goal: to generate clean knock-in strains without selection cassette

title: Prepare auxin stock solutions and plates
